1:---
2:name: convergence-gate
3:description: Adoption gate — new patterns/repos/SDKs require convergence evidence (≥3 T1 sources + ≥2 named T2 practitioners + ≥3 months stability OR strong-provenance-express predicate), else REJECT-until-convergence
4:paths: ["reports/**", ".claude/rules/**", ".claude/skills/**/SKILL.md", ".claude/skills/sota-research/**"]
5:---
6:
7:# Convergence Gate — Adopt Only When Pattern Has Converged
8:
9:# TIER-3 port provenance only: ported from Z:/claude/rules/convergence-gate.md HEAD. Parent CCC retains cycle-N audit evidence; claude-sota authority is the TIER-1/TIER-2 sources cited inside this rule.
10:
11:## The rule
12:A new pattern, repo, SDK, or external primitive is ADOPT-NOW only when CONVERGENCE evidence is present. Convergence means the pattern exists independently in multiple authoritative places, not just one. Absent convergence, the default verdict is **REJECT-until-convergence** — not STUDY-PILOT, not "maybe later."
13:
14:This gate stacks ABOVE the `.claude/skills/sota-research/SKILL.md` 5-row LOAD-BEARING bar (LOCAL — sota-research skill present at `.claude/skills/sota-research/SKILL.md`). It is stricter: the 5-row bar allows STUDY-PILOT on any `[UNKNOWN]`; the convergence gate does not — any missing convergence axis is a REJECT until that axis is satisfied OR the STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS predicate fires.
15:
16:## Convergence axes (ALL three required for ADOPT-NOW)
17:
18:| Axis | Threshold | Evidence shape |
19:|---|---|---|
20:| **Independent T1 sources** | ≥3 distinct orgs/repos/papers implementing the pattern | file:line cites in 3 different `Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/` dirs OR 3 different official docs URLs — not 3 pages of the same source |
21:| **Named T2 practitioners** | ≥2 named practitioners publicly adopting | Recognizable engineers (Karpathy / Simon Willison / Boris Cherny / Anthropic staff / equivalents), with a dated artifact (tweet, blog post, commit, conf talk) citing THIS specific pattern — not generic category endorsement |
22:| **Stability** | ≥3 months from pattern emergence to evaluation date | first public commit/post ≥90d old; <90d = "new and shiny," re-evaluate after the burn-in period (UNLESS STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS applies — see §Axis 3 5-band table) |
23:
24:Any axis failing = REJECT-until-convergence. Verdict line must name the specific missing axis + the exact evidence that would satisfy it.
25:
26:## Terminology disambiguation
27:
28:**Convergence-gate Axis 3** = **stability** (age + cpd; quantitative scalar measuring repo/pattern maturity). About: "is this pattern old enough to trust?"
29:
30:**`.claude/rules/synthesis-layer-verify.md` Subclaim-type discriminator** (UPSTREAM-CLAIM / OPERATIONAL-CLAIM / CATEGORY-CLAIM) = **claim-source classification** (qualitative shape; about what's being verified, not when). About: "which kind of evidence does this claim require?"
31:
32:Same word "axis" appears in both rules referring to different concepts. Use full names ("Axis 3 stability" vs "subclaim-type discriminator") when ambiguity matters.
33:
34:## How to apply
35:
36:Before writing any ADOPT verdict in `reports/sota-*.md` or `reports/*-audit*.md`:
37:
38:1. **List the 3 T1 sources explicitly**. If you cannot name 3 different `Z:/repos/deps/<repo>/file:line` OR 3 different official docs URLs where the pattern appears independently, the axis fails.
39:2. **Name the 2 T2 practitioners explicitly with dated artifact**. "Karpathy endorses" without a tweet URL + date is not evidence; it's wishful.
40:3. **Check the stability clock**. First commit / first public post date — `mcp__github__get_file_contents` on first-commit metadata, or the earliest blog post / paper date. <90d = candidate for STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS only (see §Axis 3); else fail.
41:4. **If ANY axis fails**, write `REJECT-until-convergence` as the verdict, with a bullet list specifying exactly what evidence would close each missing axis.
42:5. **Only then** run the sota-research 5-row bar. The convergence gate is a precondition — passing it doesn't auto-ADOPT, but failing it auto-REJECTS.
43:
44:## Evaluation methodology — concrete tools per axis
45:
84:### Axis 3 — Stability (≥3 months first-public-artifact age, scored across 5 bands)
85:
86:| Tool family | Use | Status |
87:|---|---|---|
88:| `mcp__github__get_file_contents` / commit history | `createdAt` / first-commit on the repo — repo age | ACTIVE |
89:| `mcp__exa__web_search_exa` (date range) | Earliest blog post / paper mentioning the pattern | ACTIVE |
90:| `mcp__arxiv__search_papers` + `get_abstract` | Paper publication date for research-backed patterns | ACTIVE |
91:
92:**Rule**: 90 days minimum from EARLIEST public artifact, not from the version you're looking at. A v2.0 release isn't stability evidence if v1.0 was 30 days ago.
93:
94:**Supplementary signal — commits/day (cpd)**: raw age alone under-specifies stability. A 99-day-old repo shipping 15 commits/day is structurally different from a 99-day-old repo shipping 1 commit/week — the former is still in active iteration, not burn-in. Compute `cpd = total_commits / age_days` alongside age:
95:
96:| cpd × age band | Classification | Implication |
97:|---|---|---|
98:| `cpd < 10` AND `age ≥ 90d` | Stable burn-in | Firm axis-3 PASS |
99:| `10 ≤ cpd ≤ 20` AND `90d ≤ age ≤ 180d` | Active iteration | Borderline axis-3 — PASS-with-caveat; downgrade to STUDY-PILOT or CONDITIONAL-ADOPT if axis-2 also PARTIAL |
100:| `cpd > 10` AND `age > 180d` | **Sustained active maintenance** | Firm axis-3 PASS — mature age proves stability AND velocity signals ongoing investment, NOT rewrite churn. Classic shape: high-velocity repos past burn-in (avoid misclassifying as fast-churn anti-pattern) |
101:| `cpd > 10` AND `age < 100d` | Fast-churn anti-pattern | Treat age-PASS as borderline, expect rewrites, re-audit after +90d |
102:| **STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS** (5th band, predicate-gated): `age ≥ 30d` AND axis-1 = official-org maintainership AND axis-2 = named-T2 endorsement OR maintainer-org IS T2-equivalent | **Firm axis-3 PASS — relaxed maturity gate** | When provenance is strong (org-level T1) AND a named-T2 OR org-equivalent endorsement exists, the launch-spike risk that motivates the strict 90-day gate is dominated by maintainer-org commitment. Examples of org-level T1 patterns: vercel-labs / anthropics / openai / getzep / langchain / microsoft / google / facebook-research / google-deepmind / openai-evals / equivalents. The LAUNCH-SPIKE band still applies for `unknown-org + age<90d + cpd>50` — protection holds for the truly anti-pattern cases (solo-org launch with non-permissive license = REJECT-UNTIL-CONVERGENCE unchanged) |
103:
104:The bands are exhaustive — every candidate falls into exactly one. STRONG-PROVENANCE-EXPRESS is a predicate-gated relaxation, not a default fallback; verify all three predicate clauses (≥30d age, official-org maintainer, named-T2 or org-equivalent endorsement) before applying it.
105:
106:### Fusion rule (Rider 4 discipline)
107:
108:No single tool is authoritative. Running any ONE of the above in isolation produces narrow-grep false-negatives (single-tool signal ≠ convergence). The convergence check requires ≥3 distinct tool-types returning compatible evidence — otherwise treat the finding as "one-tool signal," which is not convergence.
112:## Anti-pattern: retroactive convergence manufacturing
113:
114:Do not construct convergence evidence after choosing the verdict. The sequence must be: (1) collect convergence evidence → (2) count axes → (3) verdict. Not (1) pick verdict → (2) find supporting cites.
115:
116:If a candidate looks promising but fails convergence today, the right move is to **queue a re-audit date** (90 days out, or when a named T2 practitioner is spotted adopting it), not lower the gate.

Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:3:description: When iterative codex review (or similar adversarial reviewer) keeps surfacing finer-grained concerns on the same logical surface, decide disposition by confidence trend AND severity gate. Monotone-decline + low/medium severity → ACCEPT-WITH-DOC. Escalation OR unresolved high/critical → REVERT-AND-REMOVE. Owner-accepted high/critical → MANUAL-OVERRIDE (distinct, tracked). Stop the arc at round 5 regardless.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:29:**Critical**: stopping iteration is independent of shipping disposition. Hitting round 5 does NOT mean the surface is safe to ship — it means you've spent enough effort on layer-fix and need to switch to a terminal disposition (ACCEPT-WITH-DOC, REVERT-AND-REMOVE, or escalate to user). The terminal disposition has its OWN gates beyond iteration count.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:44:If neither holds (even at medium severity) → REVERT-AND-REMOVE or kick back to fix-iteration regardless of confidence trend. The severity gate is non-negotiable — iteration count and confidence trend alone cannot bless unresolved material findings.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:61:### Outcome B — REVERT-AND-REMOVE (escalation OR unresolved high-severity)
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:102:2. **REVERT-AND-REMOVE** if: confidence escalates between rounds (any round count), OR last-round severity is `high`/`critical` and you have no MANUAL-OVERRIDE
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:105:5. **Escalate to user** if: round ≥ 5 with high-severity unresolved finding, no clear REVERT path (e.g., feature has callers we can't easily migrate), and no owner available for MANUAL-OVERRIDE.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:113:## REVERT-then-recovery trajectory
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\closed-loop-recursive-narrowing.md:115:Outcome B (REVERT-AND-REMOVE) is not necessarily terminal for the underlying work. A common recovery shape is: REVERT removes the over-broad surface → a later, narrower fix-forward re-introduces the work with the invariant preserved + scope bounded → that narrower fix-forward converges via Outcome A (monotone-decline ACCEPT). Track the two as separate arcs (the REVERT closes arc 1; the narrower re-introduction opens arc 2) rather than as a single iteration.

7:# Synthesis-layer verify — git-diff before commit, decompose before flip
8:
9:# TIER-3 port provenance only: ported from Z:/claude/rules/synthesis-layer-verify.md HEAD. Parent CCC retains the n=9 dogfood chain and cycle-N evidence; it is not claude-sota design authority.
10:
11:At the team-lead synthesis-pre-commit gate, verify every teammate ship-report claim against `git diff` (claimed edits) and `git status` (claimed new files) BEFORE trusting the report. For new code, additionally smoke-run or import-check it. The rule applies regardless of WHY ship-report drifted — recovery pattern is invariant under failure-mode taxonomy.
12:
13:## Why
14:
15:Ship-reports drift from git reality in BOTH directions OR fail to surface a finding entirely (HONEST-NON-FINDING — see §Reporting categories), and the failure-mode taxonomy keeps growing (agent flake, proxy restart, 429 retries, Windows loopback transients, model-side stalls, infrastructure deploys mid-cycle). The synthesis-layer recovery is the same single check across all of them: `git diff` + `git status` + smoke-import. Without this check, false-failure re-spawns waste 2-5 min each; false-success commits introduce silent no-ops into git history.
16:
17:## How to apply (team-lead pre-commit checklist)
18:
19:For every claimed file edit:
20:- Run `git diff <path>` and confirm the diff matches the report's described change (additions + deletions present, not empty, not inverted).
21:
22:For every claimed new file:
23:- Run `git status --short` (or `ls -la <path>`) and confirm presence + non-zero size.
24:
25:For every new code file:
26:- Smoke-run a minimal invocation — `python -c "import <module>"`, `<hook> --help`, or at minimum re-run the project's static-analysis baseline (`pyright`, `ruff`) on the new file. File existence ≠ file imports cleanly.
27:
28:If teammate ship-report contradicts git state in EITHER direction:
29:- Do NOT commit blindly — investigate via `git reflog`, partial-write evidence, infrastructure event log, or active-task list before re-spawning or accepting.
30:
31:Anti-pattern: trusting "wrote 200 LOC across 3 files" without running `git status` to count new/changed files first.
32:
33:## SubagentStop transcript-mining (4th OVER/UNDER/HNF detection axis — iter-109 closure)
34:
35:Beyond the 3 git-state-derived axes above (`git diff` claimed edits / `git status` claimed new files / smoke-import for new code), the **SubagentStop transcript-mining axis** surfaces evidence ORTHOGONAL to git verification — what the agent CONSIDERED but DIDN'T SHIP, tool-call sequences, prompt-cache hits — visible in the subagent transcript JSONL (`agent_transcript_path` per Anthropic SDK `SubagentStopHookInput` schema at `Z:/repos/deps/claude-agent-sdk-python/src/claude_agent_sdk/types.py:309-316 @ HEAD b512f256450dba8f0dd1399e485563b7deb9c534` [VERIFIED 2026-05-02 via Ship 38 Marker Decay refresh]).
36:

Sentinel discipline per Karpathy P1 lenient-mode: `parse_status` ∈ {ok / no_transcript_path / transcript_missing / parse_empty / parse_failed}; `-1` for tool_count/tool_errors when uncertain.
38:
39:**Detection contracts**:
40:- **OVER (transcript-vs-report)**: agent's `verdict_one_line` claims `DONE: 5 fixes` but transcript shows `tool_count=2` — transcript truth refutes ship-report. Recovery: investigate via JSONL trace + revisit ship; same shape as `git diff` OVER.
41:- **UNDER (transcript surfaces unreported tool-errors)**: agent's report doesn't mention errors but transcript shows `tool_errors > 0` — agent encountered failures it suppressed. Recovery: surface the suppressed errors per cardinal-rule 7 (CLAUDE.md §Hard Rules, bullet "REPORT errors before routing around them"); pivot ship if errors load-bearing.
42:- **HONEST-NON-FINDING (transcript empty / parse failure)**: `parse_status != "ok"` — transcript missing or unparseable. Recovery: HNF disposition; do NOT re-spawn agent on the assumption transcript exists; treat axis as closed-without-finding.

52:## Reporting categories — OVER, UNDER, HONEST-NON-FINDING
53:
54:Ship-reports fall into three reporting categories at the synthesis layer, each with a distinct recovery pattern. The categories are exhaustive — every report fits one — and the recovery action differs by category.
55:
56:| Category | Definition | Synthesis-layer response |
57:|---|---|---|
58:| **OVER** | Report claims more than git shows (claimed edit reverted; claimed file absent) | `git reflog` + infrastructure event log; investigate before re-spawn or commit |
59:| **UNDER** | Report claims less than git shows (claimed nothing, file landed; partial credit) | `git diff` to surface the orphan change; accept work + correct report → commit |
60:| **HONEST-NON-FINDING** | Report says "I probed for X, found nothing" — when the brief assumed X exists | Pivot ship — DROP / REDIRECT / amend brief. The HNF IS the deliverable; do NOT re-spawn the agent to "find X anyway" |
61:
62:**Why HNF matters**: it's the highest-value report shape but easiest to mistake for "agent failed to ship." An agent that probes the brief's assumption and finds it wrong has saved a wrong-direction ship — that's a SUCCESS at the discipline layer, not a failure. The synthesis-layer recovery is to update the brief / drop the patch / redirect to the correct target — never to re-spawn under the same (now-refuted) assumption.
63:
64:**HNF as cite-vs-concept sibling**: HNF reports are often the empirical refutation of a brief-level cite-vs-concept failure. Brief asserts X exists at file:line; agent probes; X doesn't exist. Brief's assumption was a CONCEPT (loose familiarity) not a CITE (verified file:line). HNF surfaces this gap. (Cite-vs-concept semantic-equivalence remains FORWARD-REF in claude-sota; the parent CCC narrative is TIER-3 provenance only until ported with TIER-1/TIER-2 backing.)
65:
66:## Subclaim-type discriminator (UPSTREAM / OPERATIONAL / CATEGORY)
67:
68:When applying within-cycle-revision-discipline to a freshness-audit candidate, classify the SUBCLAIM by type BEFORE allocating probe budget. Three categorical types; the type predicts probe yield.
69:
70:| Subclaim type | Definition | Probe yield |
71:|---|---|---|
72:| **UPSTREAM-CLAIM** | About external project's state (README content, repo metadata, framing) — subject to upstream evolution between verdict-cycle and probe-cycle | HIGH refutation candidate — upstream may have reformed |
73:| **OPERATIONAL-CLAIM** | About OUR harness state (live MCP invocations, hook-fire counts, integration depth) — controlled by us, slow-moving | LOW refutation likelihood — state changes only when we change it |
74:| **CATEGORY-CLAIM** | About semantic mismatch between candidate and our use-case (RAG vs session-memory, batch vs streaming) — requires upstream pivot to flip | LOW refutation likelihood — categorical signals stable |
75:
76:**Mixed types**: a single candidate's subclaim chain can include all three. CATEGORY-CLAIM ("API-redundant with X") + OPERATIONAL-CLAIM ("our X integration is live") can both apply to the same exclusion verdict.
77:
78:**How to apply (pre-probe budget allocation)**:
79:1. Type the claim — UPSTREAM / OPERATIONAL / CATEGORY?
80:2. Estimate probe budget — UPSTREAM gets full 5-axis (WebFetch README + GitHub API + convergence-gate axes); OPERATIONAL gets spot-check via local grep; CATEGORY gets one-pass README scan
81:3. Honest classification — if uncertain, default to UPSTREAM-CLAIM (under-probing has higher false-PASS cost than over-probing)
82:
83:**Distinguishes from §Reporting categories above**: §Reporting categories classifies REPORT shape (OVER/UNDER/HNF — about agent's output). §Subclaim-type discriminator classifies SOURCE shape (UPSTREAM/OPERATIONAL/CATEGORY — about what's being verified). Orthogonal axes — a UPSTREAM-CLAIM probe may produce HNF, OVER, or UNDER report.
84:
85:## Output-form verification modifier (SHAPE-CLAIM)
86:
87:After typing the subclaim by source as UPSTREAM / OPERATIONAL / CATEGORY, add **SHAPE-CLAIM** when the claim depends on **structured output that can be checked before deployment**: TypeScript workflow code, Pydantic / BaseModel payloads, Zod / Effect schemas, JSON Schema validated tool args, `PINS.json` entries, `settings.json` hook entries, `.mcp.json` server configs, MCP tool args, or hook JSONL payloads.
88:
89:**SHAPE-CLAIM is a MODIFIER, not a source type.** It combines with each source class:
90:- `UPSTREAM-CLAIM + SHAPE-CLAIM`: PINS.json bumps citing upstream HEAD SHA + content-SHA (the bump is upstream-state; the content shape is checkable)
91:- `OPERATIONAL-CLAIM + SHAPE-CLAIM`: settings.json hook entries, .mcp.json server configs, hook JSONL payloads (the hook fires per harness state; the JSON shape validates)
92:- `CATEGORY-CLAIM + SHAPE-CLAIM`: agent frontmatter or skill SKILL.md (the frontmatter is structured + parseable; the categorical role is semantic)
93:
94:**Probe rule**: run the strongest available compile/schema/validation check first. If it passes, downgrade only **shape-refutation budget**; still run semantic/runtime probes for side effects, credentials, provider limitations, type coercion, `any`/untyped fields, unsupported schema keywords, and producer/consumer boundary mismatches. **Compile-pass is NOT deploy-pass.**

104:**Anti-patterns** (per codex T1 F-002 + Q7 prescription):
105:- **Free-form JSON when a schema/compiler exists** — n8n catches this; "code beats JSON" for LLM-emitted structured output

122:

148:## Edge cases
149:
150:- **Pure doc-memo writes by trusted teammates**: `git diff` is cheap (~1s) and catches missing frontmatter, partial renders, accidental indentation breakage. Run anyway — discipline is unconditional, not trust-tier gated.
151:- **File looks present but doesn't compile**: a common UNDER-report failure mode. A `Write` can land successfully (size > 0) yet content has a syntax error from partial render. ALWAYS pair `git status` (presence) with smoke-import (`python -c "import X"`) for new Python files.
152:- **Race conditions on background-spawned agents**: when Task notifications arrive mid-prompt, the next `git diff` probe might catch in-flight Edit/Write calls. Solution: check active TaskList before committing.
153:- **Intentional reverts shipped as the deliverable**: if teammate output IS a `git revert` or `git reset`, the diff direction inverts — verify the revert was the intended action, not an unintended rollback of prior work.
154:- **Infrastructure-coincident failures**: when a teammate fails during a known infrastructure event (proxy restart, service deploy, network blip), the `git diff` probe is THE primary signal because the agent's ship-report channel is exactly what the infrastructure event broke — DO NOT downgrade verification confidence just because the failure has a plausible non-agent cause.
155:- **Authority-source summary mistaken for verification**: when a teammate / primary-doc / report says "X confirmed", verify which LAYER they confirmed. Summary at L1 ≠ verification at L2-L5. Especially load-bearing when team-lead summary appears to authorize a verdict-flip.
156:- **Promotion-ship dogfood**: when promoting a feedback memory to a rule, the brief itself can carry the same drift the rule guards against. Critic should self-disclose unverified instance attributions; team-lead should spot-check brief cites against original cycle artifacts before applying.
157:- **Files outside the git tree** (e.g., `~/.codex/config.toml`, `Z:/repos/deps/<X>/` checkouts): the `git diff` check doesn't apply directly; substitute with `cp` backup before edit + post-edit Read-back to verify content matches intent.

49:## NEW Cardinal Rule for this runtime (cardinal-rule-6 fresh-from-github + official-native-channel)
50:
51:6. **Pull from newest GitHub before install via OFFICIAL NATIVE CHANNEL ONLY.** Every install command MUST first refresh upstream AND use the canonical official install primitive (no workarounds, no third-party mirrors, no shell-script wrappers around official commands):
52:   - `npm install -g <pkg>@latest` from `https://registry.npmjs.org` (official npm registry; NOT pinned-old-version, NOT mirror)

56:   - `docker pull <image>:latest` from official Docker Hub OR explicit registry
57:   - `/plugin marketplace add <official-marketplace-url>` then `/plugin install <pkg>` (Anthropic-canonical marketplace mechanism)

After every `os.open`, the caller MUST: (i) read `current_mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.fstat(fd).st_mode)`; (ii) if `current_mode != mode` AND the file is owned by caller-uid, call `os.fchmod(fd, mode)` to coerce existing file to the mode invariant; (iii) if `os.fchmod` raises (`PermissionError` due to read-only mount, alien owner, ACL conflict on Windows NTFS, etc.), FAIL CLOSED — propagate the exception rather than proceeding with non-conforming perms (the audit-trail invariant is enforced everywhere or fails loudly). The `O_CREAT` flag ensures a missing log auto-creates rather than failing the first writer; **if `os.open` raises (read-only mount, permission denied, disk full), the exception MUST propagate — do not catch-and-ignore** (per Round-5 F-1 silent-failure finding). Take an **exclusive advisory lock** (`fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX)` on POSIX / `msvcrt.locking` on Windows); **if neither primitive is available, or if the platform does not enforce advisory locks (e.g., NFS without NLM support), FAIL CLOSED — raise rather than proceeding without a lock** (per Round-5 F-2 NFS-silent-succeed finding). **Windows separate-lockfile mechanism** *(Round-7c per T3 round-7b NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `48c49fb` caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE)*: `msvcrt.locking` locks `nbytes` from CURRENT file-pointer position, NOT the whole file like POSIX `fcntl.flock`. Under O_APPEND the JSONL fd's pointer moves on each write, breaking lock-release symmetry (LK_UNLCK at the new pointer would find no lock at the byte LK_LOCK was issued for). Round-7b workaround (shipped at `scripts/_atomic_jsonl_append.py:_acquire_lock(fd, path)` commit `48c49fb`): open separate `<jsonl-path>.lock` file with 1-byte placeholder + lock byte 0 of the LOCKFILE (no writes to lockfile means file pointer stays at byte 0). Module returns `lock_fd` for Windows callers to release; `None` for POSIX. **Lock-protocol rollout constraint** *(Round-7c per same T3 finding)*: when the lock protocol bumps (direct-jsonl-fd → separate-lockfile-v1, or separate-lockfile-v1 → separate-lockfile-v2-versioned), enforce single-version deployment for the entire concurrent-writer cohort. Old + new code locking DIFFERENT lock domains do NOT mutually exclude — concurrent writers can race even though each ALONE acquires its lock correctly. Mitigations (pick ONE before any concurrent rollout): **(i) transitional dual-lock**: acquire both old AND new protocol locks in series during the transition window; **(ii) runtime version-marker**: write protocol-version byte to lockfile + fail-closed on read-version-mismatch (FORWARD-REF for v2 lock protocol bump); **(iii) single-version cohort barrier**: coordinate cohort upgrade via deployment system before any new-version runs. Currently sss has ZERO consumers of `_atomic_jsonl_append.py` (FORWARD-REF wire-up Ships 2-5 pending per `tmp/wave22-orchestrator-salvage-jsonl-mode-bits-audit-2026-05-05.md`), so the version-skew window is THEORETICAL until first hook migrates to use the module. Future protocol bumps MUST honor one of (i)/(ii)/(iii). HOLD the lock across BOTH (a) JSON-encoding the record AND (b) the single low-level `os.write(fd, encoded_bytes)` — never use buffered text writes (`f.write(json.dumps(rec) + \"\\n\")` via Python file objects can split into multiple writes). **If JSON encoding raises (`UnicodeEncodeError`, non-serializable type), release the lock and propagate the exception — do not silently drop the record** (per Round-5 F-3 silent-record-drop finding). For records where **`len(encoded_bytes)` — the byte count AFTER JSON encoding, NOT the key count of the dict —** exceeds the platform atomic-write bound (≤PIPE_BUF 4KB POSIX; ≤512 bytes for Windows or treat the lock as the sole correctness boundary), reject the record OR shard via option (b) filename-namespace; do NOT silently truncate (per Round-5 F-5 measurement-target finding). After the write, `os.fsync(fd)` if durability is part of the contract (audit-trail JSONL needs fsync; ephemeral telemetry may skip); **if `os.fsync` raises (`EIO`, `ENOSPC`), propagate the exception — do not silently ignore a durability failure when durability is contracted** (per Round-5 F-4 fsync-failure finding). 63:## Weighted Quality Rubric (S25/M20/C25/Co15/L10/P5)
64:
65:| Dimension | Weight | Formula |
66:|---|---|---|
67:| Security | 25% | `0.5 × Scorecard/10 + 0.3 × (1 − grype_high_cve_rate) + 0.2 × best-practices-badge {0, 0.7, 0.85, 1}` |
68:| Maintenance | 20% | `0.5 × min(commits_90d/100, 1) + 0.3 × contributors_active + 0.2 × Scorecard.Maintained/10` |
69:| Capability | 25% | Subjective 0-1 from skill-creator A/B eval pass-rate |
70:| Community | 15% | `0.4 × min(log10(stars)/5, 1) + 0.3 × forks_velocity + 0.3 × issue_response_time_inv` |
71:| License | 10% | `{MIT/Apache/BSD = 1, MPL = 0.7, LGPL = 0.5, GPL = 0.2 if compatible else 0}` |
72:| Performance | 5% | Micro-benchmarks if applicable, else neutral 0.5 |
73:
74:### Trust weights (input reliability)
75:| Input | Weight |
76:|---|---|
77:| Personal A/B eval | 0.40 |
78:| OpenSSF Scorecard | 0.20 |
79:| Snyk Advisor | 0.15 |
80:| Bus-factor | 0.10 |
81:| deps.dev | 0.10 |
82:| Stars / forks | 0.05 |
83:
84:### Sensitivity check
85:Re-run weighted scoring with weights ±5%; final ranking MUST be stable to count as confident selection.
86:
87:### Hard rules
88:- Penalize last-commit > 90d (Maintenance × 0.5)
89:- Require ≥1 commit last-30d to mark "active"
90:- Halve community weight when contributors_active < 3
91:- Reject Scorecard.Maintained < 5
92:- Reject bus-factor 1 + no last-90d commits

96:## 11-Step Research Workflow
97:
98:1. **DEFINE** the problem with explicit success criteria + verification rubric
99:2. **DISCOVER** ≥4 distinct source cohorts (L1 stack): GitHub MCP + Exa + Perplexity + Firecrawl + OSSInsight + DeepWiki + ≥1 leaderboard
100:3. **TRIAGE** via gh repo metadata + Star History + Scorecard quick-score; cut candidate list to ≤10
101:4. **DEEP EVAL** via L3 stack (Snyk + deps.dev + OSV-Scanner + Trivy + Syft+Grype + Semgrep + Serena LSP)
102:5. **SEMANTIC** Q&A via DeepWiki + RepoMix compressed dump + ast-grep symbol probes
103:6. **BENCHMARK** via custom task harness from real tickets + skill-creator A/B + Inspect AI + promptfoo + deepeval
104:7. **COMPARE** via `comparison-matrix.md` weighted-rubric scoring + sensitivity ±5%
105:8. **SELECT** + write log4brains MADR ADR archiving all rejected alternatives with reasons
106:9. **HANDOFF** to L7 Construction via `findings.md` + Spec-Kit constitution `## Selected SOTA Dependencies`
107:10. **BUILD** complex project using ONLY SOTA repos selected; cite each at version-pinned reference
108:11. **FEEDBACK** via L8 observability (Langfuse + Splitrail + claude_telemetry) + post-mortem ADRs + rubric weight updates
109:

111:
112:## Failure Modes + Mitigations
113:
114:| Failure mode | Mitigation |
115:|---|---|
116:| Star bias | Cap stars 5% weight; require Scorecard + Snyk + custom eval to corroborate |
117:| Stale benchmarks (SWE-bench saturated; Mythos 93.9% / Opus 4.7 87.6%) | Use Inspect AI on YOUR task suite + skill-creator A/B against real project work; NEVER quote leaderboard ≥85% as verdict |
118:| SWE-ABS 19.78% false positives; METR merge-rate ~24pp below benchmark scores | Apply benchmark-discount factor; trust personal A/B over public leaderboard |
119:| Prompt injection (Snyk ToxicSkills Feb 2026: 36% of public Agent Skills have injection) | Apply Lethal Trifecta filter (private data + untrusted tokens + exfiltration vector); read README via Serena symbol view or RepoMix compressed dump (NOT full clone); `.claudeignore` for secrets; SHA-256 plan attestation |
120:| Hallucinated repos | `gh repo view owner/repo` verification BEFORE any citation; reject if 404 |
121:| License pollution | SPDX scan in CI; allowlist enforced in repo-evaluate; copyleft → 0 if proprietary, 0.2 if open |
122:| Maintainer abandonment | Scorecard.Maintained < 5 → reject; bus-factor 1 + no last-90d commits → reject; Sigstore-signed commits required for high-trust deps |
123:| MCP supply-chain | Install only from claude-plugins-official OR repos with ≥1000 stars + recent commits + Sigstore signed + no opaque post-install scripts; run mcp-scan if available |
124:| YOLO mode drift | NEVER `--dangerously-skip-permissions` outside isolated CI; CR-7 Phase 1 permission classifier defaults |
